NOTES carried forward, still relevant for any future work in this repo: (1) sequence .mmd sources are NOT persisted; (2) sequence renders live in their OWNING ISSUE's folder; (3) renders.lock can go stale silently after an as-built XML edit - re-run `python audit.py --record-renders` at close; (4) map.yaml's ucs: lists must be real workbook UC codes only, never an issue id; (5) IndexedStack-based navigation means every FloatingActionButton needs an explicit unique heroTag - six across the app as of FEAT04, check for collisions before adding more; (6) a clean local audit.py pass does NOT prove CI will pass - only the actual CI log surfaces a glob()-ordering-dependent bug (fixed 2026-08-23); (7) BEFORE writing a new screen/class, check the relevant class diagram has a box for it - flutter-coder halting on FEAT04's AccountsScreen is the model to follow; a genuinely private per-file widget or plain top-level function (like FEAT05's _CategoryAutocompleteField, FEAT09/FEAT10's group_style.dart/kind_style.dart/tab_app_bar_actions.dart, or FEAT11's _PersonAccountField) does NOT need a diagram entry - check whether the new thing is a tracked class (Screen/Provider/DAO/Notifier) or private/shared implementation detail before halting; (8) this project is a pilot run for a different target project (owner's own words, 2026-08-24) - the process trail itself is part of what gets extracted later, so keep the same discipline on these post-backlog polish items as on the original tracked issues; (9) a plain ListView(children: [...]) in a widget test does NOT build off-screen children automatically (Sliver-realized, not eager) - a widget test asserting on content below the fold must scroll first (tester.drag + pumpAndSettle), caught repeatedly across FEAT07/FEAT10's chart/card tests; (10) a subagent can hit its own session/usage limit mid-task and terminate without finishing - check `git status`/diff for partial, uncommitted work before assuming a 'failed' task notification means nothing was done; FEAT07's coder got the DAO layer fully done and correct before terminating, and that work was kept and built on rather than redone; (11) `flutter gen-l10n` is a SEPARATE required step from `dart run build_runner build` whenever an ARB file changes - build_runner alone leaves new l10n keys undefined and flutter analyze fails on undefined_getter; now documented in context/coding-conventions/dart-and-flutter.md; (12) when two issues both touch the same file (e.g. FEAT09 and FEAT10 both touch balance_sheet_screen.dart), dispatch their flutter-coder agents SEQUENTIALLY, not in parallel, to avoid two agents editing the same working-tree file at once; (13) not every enum-value addition is a schema migration - a textEnum column with no CHECK constraint accepts a new legal Dart-side value with nothing more than a build_runner regen; check for a CHECK constraint before reaching for drift_dev make-migrations (FEAT11); (14) `ref.read` inside a helper does NOT subscribe the calling widget to anything - if a value needs to update as a stream emits, something in build() must `ref.watch` it too, even if the read itself happens elsewhere (FEAT11's repay-direction-toggle default stayed stuck until this was added); (15) when a visual bug report is ambiguous or hard to picture from text/a screenshot alone, connect to the owner's already-running debug build (mcp__dart__dtd to find/connect the DTD instance, adb for screenshots and uiautomator dump for exact widget bounds since guessed pixel coordinates repeatedly miss) and reproduce it live before touching code - this caught that two of three reported issues (FEAT11's toggle/checkbox) were not bugs at all, just untriggered preconditions, and confirmed the third (the SegmentedButton overflow) precisely before fixing it); (16) after force-stopping a running debug app to fix an unrelated issue (e.g. a bad tap coordinate), relaunching it via adb (monkey/am start) brings back the LAST INSTALLED APK, not the latest source - a hot reload only patches an already-running Dart VM, so once that process is killed, only a fresh  rebuild reflects new code; this silently showed a stale screen once (FEAT12) until caught by re-verifying with a clean rebuild rather than trusting the first screenshot.
